summary: Brad Bradford's Instagram record positions housing as his signature issue, framed as a supply-and-affordability crisis requiring faster construction, less red tape, and lower government-imposed costs. Bradford supports expanded "missing middle" housing, sixplexes, mid-rise on Avenues, laneway and garden suites, modular and rapid-build construction, office-to-residential conversion, and purpose-built rental. He opposes exclusionary zoning, the angular plane rule, high development charges (citing 1200% growth since 2010), the Vacant Home Tax's reverse-onus design, and Mayor Chow's luxury home tax and public builder approach as insufficient. Bradford has moved motions to cut development charges 25%, streamline modular approvals, expand major-street unit caps to 60, and double the first-time homebuyer rebate. He also champions supportive housing with wraparound services, citing three shelter/supportive housing sites delivered in his ward.

key_positions.stance: Supports building more housing supply broadly, including missing middle, mid-rise, sixplexes, laneway/garden suites, and purpose-built rental
Opposes high development charges and government-imposed housing costs, calling for cuts to fees to spur construction
Supports cutting red tape, streamlining approvals, and updating zoning bylaws to enable more housing
Supports supportive housing with wraparound mental health, addiction, and job supports as a long-term solution to homelessness
Opposes the Vacant Home Tax's reverse-onus structure requiring homeowners to annually prove residency
Opposes Mayor Chow's luxury home tax and public builder approach, arguing they add costs without delivering housing
Supports modular and rapid-build construction technologies to accelerate housing delivery
Supports ending exclusionary zoning and adding gentle density in existing neighbourhoods
Supports doubling first-time homebuyer rebate and increasing land transfer tax rebate thresholds
Supports converting underutilized office space into housing
